chunks: Then man will be told what he had sent ahead (of good) and what he had left behind.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about being informed of one's deeds on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Qiyamah underscores the precision of divine accounting, where 'what he sent forward' refers to accumulated merits and sins, while 'what he left behind' often denotes neglected duties or delayed repentance. The Imam Ali (AS) tradition highlights that this notification serves as a direct confirmation of individual responsibility, emphasizing that no deed, however small, is concealed from the All-Knowing. This reinforces the concept of 'Hisab' (accounting) as a moment of absolute clarity where the soul confronts the tangible reality of its choices.
